dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1791 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json), and again with the families of 1790 over the 1791 pages (items_from_1790.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was compared by machine with every page and counted again by its opening; a sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers found the runs no finder item covers, and they were read. Counted item by item (80 entries, the daily proceedings of Congress left out as digests), 67 items meet the bar (count_1791.md); where an item's family or run also holds other texts (the acts of Congress share their formulas), its papers were counted by its own words. The admitted and chosen items were counted again by their own words over all 1,242 pages in both transcriptions, and read on every page.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended on 23 November 2026, the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; as in R-01, the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35); one affair's items as in X-1800-01; digests are not admitted; sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) as in every year. In 1791 4 to 6 papers survive for an item's weeks, so the bar is 4 for every item.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1791 has 6 catalogue series, which are 6 papers: the Gazette of the United States (107 issues), the New-Hampshire Gazette (53), the New Hampshire Gazetteer (49) and the Patowmac Guardian (49) through the year; the Kentucky Gazette (41), with no issue from 23 July to 8 October; and the National Gazette (18) from 31 October. No 1791 issue has a corrected date; the release's map lists 3 misfiled RevX pages of 1791 (the New-Hampshire Gazette of 12 February and 1 September), none of them a page of this ledger.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Of 67 items eligible by the count, 6 are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks, counted by their own words, and are admitted: the battle near Carpentras (5 of 5), the treaty at Newtown Point, the plague in Turkey, the Birmingham paragraph and the Danville letter on General Wilkinson's express (4 of 4, in the weeks when no Kentucky Gazette survives), and the King of France's letter accepting the constitution (6 of 6, in three translations). 16 are chosen; the others are listed as not chosen, except four items on private persons, listed for the owner.
counted_item_by_item.The acts of Congress by their own words: The automatic families join the acts of the session by their formulas ('Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives'); counted by each act's opening, the acts on Kentucky, on Vermont and on another regiment are in 4 papers each, and the excise act, the Bank's supplementary act and the act fixing the next meeting of Congress in 3 (below the bar); pages that only recite an act's title, such as the New-Hampshire Gazette's list of the session's acts of 16 June, are not counted (C-07).
counted_item_by_item.Printed forms counted together: General Scott's letter to the Secretary of War and the Lexington 'detail of facts' that gives it in the third person; the letter from Paris on the importation of oil as an extract and as a report of it; the King of France's letter in three translations; the paragraph on the schooner Hardy in a Philadelphia and a New York form (C-02).
counted_item_by_item.The window of the Danville letter: The Danville letter is printed from 17 September to 7 October; the Kentucky Gazette's next issue after 23 July is of 8 October, the day after the letter's three weeks (Y-THIN counts the first printing's day and the 20 days after it). So 4 papers survive for its weeks, and the letter, printed by all 4, is admitted.
